This method can be used to bypass _is_regexp_spam(): https://shkspr.mobi/blog/2018/11/domain-hacks-with-unusual-unicode-characters/

Post a comment containing http://bit。ly/foo.

idn_to_ascii() could be used to normalize text before checking it with the regex.

items.content_html:
Problem

Some requirements of a format are absolute: no option should let a caller turn them off. The packages don't treat them that way today.

  • File.vCard: VcardReader reads a card with no VERSION line when AllowMissingRequiredProperties is set. SourceVersion is then null, so the 4.0 conformance checks never run (a card with two N properties and PREF=999 is returned). One relaxation turns off every other check, which AGENTS.md "Standards compliance" forbids: a deviation must never turn on as a side effect of another option.
  • File.iCal: AllowMissingRequiredProperties is documented as covering a missing VERSION on read.

VERSION doesn't just have to be present. It selects the grammar used to read everything else (vCard 2.1, 3.0 and 4.0 lex differently). With none, the reader has no basis for reading the data.

Policy

An element is absolute if it meets either test:

  1. It selects how everything else is read: the format's identity, grammar, encoding or framing.
  2. If it is wrong on output, it breaks the structure of the file or lets a value change it.

When a source (input or output) breaks an absolute requirement, or a combination of options or any other means would make a reader or writer break one, the reader or writer throws on the attempted action. No option waives it. The exception message names the rule and cites the RFC section, and the exception is distinguishable from one an Allow* option can waive, so a caller isn't told to set an option that won't help.

Candidate absolute requirements (to verify against each RFC before implementing)

  • BEGIN/END pairing and matching component names (vCard, iCalendar, nested components).
  • VERSION present, with a value the package implements (vCard 2.1, 3.0, 4.0; iCalendar 2.0, RFC 5545 section 3.7.4).
  • VERSION position and cardinality in vCard 4.0 (RFC 6350 section 6.7.9: one, immediately after BEGIN). Check the 2.1 and 3.0 wording. This includes the second-VERSION lexing bug in #849.
  • Content-line syntax: a property name is a token, a parameter has =, a value has no raw control characters.
  • Writer: escaping of text values and quoting of parameter values, so a written value can never change the structure of the output. The iCal writer already refuses an unquoted :, ; or ,; audit the rest in both packages.
  • Folding never splits a character.
  • Character encoding where the standard fixes it (vCard 4.0, iCalendar default UTF-8). vCard 2.1 and 3.0 allow CHARSET.
  • jCal/xCal and jCard/xCard root structure and namespace.

Not absolute, and staying under the existing Allow* options: other required properties (PRODID, UID, DTSTAMP, FN, N), CRLF line breaks, the byte order mark, and anything else a reader can interpret unambiguously.

Scope and compatibility

  • File.vCard is v2.0 and unreleased in this respect, so this can land as a bug fix.
  • File.iCal v1.0.0 is released. Rejecting a VERSION-less calendar whatever the options are is a breaking change, so that part waits for v2.0 (Release-note: breaking).
  • Each item needs a test showing the exception under every option combination that could reach it, for reader and writer.
  • This replaces review finding 1 (the missing-VERSION conformance bypass) from the vCard package review.

Found by a code review of File.vCard at d52e789 and discussion of its options.
items.title: File.vCard, File.iCal: throw on input or output that breaks an absolute format requirement, whatever the options

Polls! #395 is for just rendering them; the next step would be to let people actually post and vote in them.

Sadly, as of 9/2023, they're mostly incomplete across Bridgy Fed's protocols:

  • ActivityPub: done, pretty commonly used; example poll
  • IndieWeb: incomplete, not much ongoing development
  • Bluesky: not yet designed
  • Nostr: NIP-69 isn't yet in the main NIPs repo, depends on zaps 🫤, very little adoption

items.content_html:
Why

Adds a per-bot webmentions option in feeds.yml (default true) and sets it to false for terence_eden, whose owner asked not to receive them. Closes #306.

Opted-out bots send no post, reaction, or retraction webmentions but still cache reacting profiles for their post pages (src/lib/webmentions.ts). The README and /about now cover webmentions, both opt-outs, robots.txt, and every public page.

Risks

Mentions already sent to shkspr.mobi stay until removed there, since opted-out bots send no retractions.
items.title: feat(webmentions): let feeds opt out of webmentions
